extracted.intended_audience: education researchers, policymakers, and elementary-school educators (grade 5 writing)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating grade-5 student writing using the 6+1 Trait Writing model, including both a single holistic score for overall writing quality and analytic six-trait six-point scoring for individual trait measures, plus guidance on professional development implementation and scoring fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas (Trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ideas trait includes the main content and message, including supporting details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates the clarity, focus, and development of the main idea and the presence and relevance of supporting detail as a core characteristic of writing quality within the 6+1 framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization (Trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization refers to the structure and logical flow of the writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses the overall structure, sequencing, transitions, and coherence of the piece — how effectively the writing's parts fit together to present the idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice (Trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice includes the perspective and style of the individual writer and his or her orientation toward the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures the writer's presence, authenticity, and appropriateness of tone for the intended audience; part of the six core characteristics used in analytic scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word Choice (Trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: Word Choice addresses the variety, precision, and evocativeness of the language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates vocabulary selection, specificity, and imagery that makes the writing expressive and exact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence Fluency (Trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentence Fluency includes the rhythm, flow, and sound patterns in the construction of sentences that may make them pleasant and interesting to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses how sentences are constructed for flow and readability, including variation in sentence length and structure and how well sentences move the reader through the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions (Trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Conventions trait, sometimes called mechanics, includes spelling, punctuation, grammar, capitalization, and other rule-based language forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures correctness and control of standard English conventions; critical for clarity though sometimes separated from higher-level traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation (Trait; the '+1')
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation is focused on page layout and formatting issues and is related to the visual aspects of publishing writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically applied when writing is carried through to publication or classroom presentation; not usually measured in large-scale assessments because such assessments require particular formatting. (Described as the +1 in the 6+1 model.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic Rubric / Holistic Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Each essay was rated using a single 'holistic' score for overall writing quality; the holistic score was used for the confirmatory analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an overall judgment of writing quality that aggregates multiple dimensions; used as the primary outcome for the main (confirmatory) effectiveness analysis in the study. Scoring procedures included blinding and quality-control (see Appendix G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic Rubrics — Six-Trait / Six-Point Analytical Scoring Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: An analytic scoring guide that rates each of the six core traits on a six-point scale (six-trait/six-point guide).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trait-specific scores produced by the analytic rubric were used for exploratory analyses of impacts on particular writing traits (ideas, organization, voice, word choice, sentence fluency, conventions). Details of the analytic rubrics and scoring anchors are in Appendix E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of Effective Adolescent Writing Instruction (selected)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended classroom practices synthesized from experimental studies: have students analyze models of good writing; explicitly teach strategies for planning, revising, and editing; involve students in collaborative use of writing strategies; assign specific goals for each writing project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These practices (from Graham & Perin meta-analysis) are treated as core components of the intervention and serve as instructional-quality criteria for what effective writing instruction should include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fidelity of Implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement of the extent to which teachers implemented the practices recommended by the 6+1 Trait model, primarily via teacher self-report surveys at three points during the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fidelity is evaluated through teacher-reported use of specific classroom practices (baseline, midyear, end-of-year). The report notes the survey instrument does not provide easily interpretable magnitudes of difference or precise levels of implementation; professional development format and timing (3-day summer institute + three one-day workshops) are described as the mechanism for promoting implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring Procedures and Quality Control (rater blindness and reliability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures to ensure unbiased, reliable scoring: data management that kept the research team blind to essay origin during scoring; essay raters were blind to whether an essay was pretest or posttest and whether it came from treatment or control schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring quality-control measures, interrater reliability statistics, and coding details are reported (Appendix G). These procedural standards are criteria for trustworthy outcome measurement in the study's evaluation design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten Trait-Based Classroom Strategies (Appendix reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix A includes 'Ten trait-based classroom strategies' as part of the professional development and classroom implementation guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although detailed strategies are in Appendix A, the existence of an enumerated set of classroom strategies functions as prescriptive instructional criteria for implementing the 6+1 model in classrooms.
